dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise.

Hi, yeah, hi. My name's Marisa Fortes, and I'm calling about the water on my street, it's, okay, so it's bad. I'm at 52 Mill Street, up in Historic Hill. And I'm sorry if there's noise, I'm on my cell, I'm standing in a line.
That's fine, I can hear you. What's the water doing at Mill Street?

So the drain at the corner is just not taking anything. The water is over the curb and all the way across the sidewalk, like I can't even get to my own front steps without wading. And this is from the rain today, the soaker that's hitting right now. It started this morning and it hasn't let up.
Okay. Is it the storm drain right in front of your building, or down at the corner?

Corner, well, kind of in between. It's by the corner. Okay, so, funny story, my cousin said the same thing happened at her place over in Middletown last month, her whole parking lot, but that's her thing, whatever, that's not why I'm calling. Anyway. Where was I. The drain. Yes.
The drain by the corner. Is it clogged with leaves, or is it just full of water?

Both, honestly. There's a pile of wet leaves sitting on top of it like a blanket. And the water's pooling and pooling. And then, oh, this is the part that got me, a delivery truck came down, one of those big box trucks, and it tried to go through and it got stuck. Like stuck stuck. The driver was out there on his phone for like twenty minutes.
Is the truck still there?

Um, it was when I left, like ten minutes ago. I had to leave because I have to catch the ferry, and I'm in this line and it is moving so slow. Like they said it'd be a few minutes and it's been forever. Sorry. Okay. So the truck is partly blocking the lane too, so now cars are trying to squeeze by and splashing everybody.
Got it. Is anybody in danger, any cars stalled in deep water, anyone hurt?

No one hurt. But I'm honestly worried, because there's kids who walk down that street, the school bus lets out a couple blocks up, and the dog walkers, there's so many people with dogs on that street, and they're walking right along the edge of that water. You can't tell how deep it is near the drain. Somebody's going to step in the wrong spot, or a car's going to throw a wave at a kid.
Yeah, that's a fair worry. I'm going to put this in as an urgent drain call so a crew can get out there and clear it.

Okay. Because this isn't new, is the thing. That corner always backs up whenever it rains hard, and it just sits there. You'd think somebody would have fixed it by now. My landlord says it's the city's drain, and the city says, I don't even know what the city says, nobody ever says anything.
I hear you. I can't tell you exactly when the crew will get there, they're stretched thin in a storm like this, but this will go on the list as a flooded roadway with a blocked drain.
Right, right. Sorry, can you hear me? The line is, I'm going through the, hold on. [line breaks up] Can you hear me now?
I can hear you. You're at 52 Mill Street, drain by the corner, water across the sidewalk and into the lane, truck stuck.

Yes, exactly. That's it. And the leaves, put the leaves. Can I ask for a call back? When it's done, when they've actually cleared it. Because I don't want to just assume and then come home tonight and it's still a lake.
Sure. What's the best number?
It's 401-555-0186. That's my cell.
401-555-0186. I'll note it to call you once the work is done.
Thank you. Seriously. I know it's pouring and everybody's calling, I just, it keeps happening and I'm tired of watching it. Okay, the line is finally moving. I've got to go.
Go catch your ferry. If the water gets worse or anything changes with that truck, call us back, and if it's an emergency, call 911.
Okay. Thanks, Denise. Bye.
